items.review_rationale: Reviewed mutual independence for arbitrary indexed family of events using every finite index subset, including singleton and empty-index product conventions, not merely pairwise tests.

references.context: Choice of one measurable event in the common sigma algebra for every index i in arbitrary index set I.
Finite collection of distinct indices from the possibly infinite index set I.
Event shared by all A_j for indices j in J, equal to Omega for J empty.
Product of real numbers P(A_j) over the finite set J, interpreted as one if J empty.

references.disposition: For three or more events every finite joint intersection must satisfy product identity, not only pairs.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed pairwise independence as product rule required for each two distinct indices in common probability space, with explicit distinction from full mutual independence.

references.context: Collection of events indexed by a set I and belonging to a shared sigma algebra.
Only pairs of different members of the index set are tested.

references.disposition: Higher-order joint independence is not guaranteed by the pairwise product conditions.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed finite simple cycle as cyclic vertex sequence of length k>=3 in loopless simple undirected graph, with distinct interior vertices and every successive edge present.

references.context: Ordered finite list v_0 to v_(k-1) closed by return to starting vertex.
Apart from repeated final starting vertex, no two vertices at indices 0 through k-1 coincide.
For every index i, unordered pair of v_i and v_(i+1 mod k) belongs to graph edge set.
Wrap index k-1 back to index zero in cyclic adjacency formula.

references.disposition: Loopless simple graph cannot have loops or two-edge repeated walks as simple cycles.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed connectedness as absence of separation into two disjoint nonempty open subsets covering X, valid even for the empty topological space.

references.context: Members of topology tau on the same ambient set X.
Their union equals the entire underlying space.
Both candidate open sets contain at least one point.

references.disposition: No separation of the empty space into two nonempty opens exists, so empty space is connected under this source convention.
